targets.title: The aging of the social mind – differential effects on components of social understanding
targets.evidence_quote: Therefore, the object of this study was to replicate the effect of age on empathy, compassion and ToM found in the study of Reiter et al . [ 62 ] by using the same paradigm (EmpaToM) in a different setting (inside an MRI scanner) and in an independent sample of YA and OA but keeping all other methods as close as possible to the original study.
targets.outcome_quote: Concerning ToM we replicated the effect of age on ToM accuracy—showing a decline in ToM performance in OA compared with YA. Age differences with respect of ToM are of notable interest given comparable educational attainment levels in YA and OA in the current sample (coherent with Reiter et al .’s sample [ 62 ]). This speaks against the notion proposed by several authors [ 85 , 86 ] that age differences in perspective taking are mediated through differing educational levels in these cohorts. However, we did not replicate the effect of age on ToM reaction time.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The final synthesis explicitly confirms accuracy and rejects the reaction-time effect. The broad abstract refers to preserved affect and declining cognition; the qualified overall statement that they mainly succeeded is consistent with partial replication rather than an unconditional overall success verdict.
